cohort: The study participants are individuals (mothers) from nationally representative demographic and health surveys in Zimbabwe, leveraging individual-level variation in birth timing.
finding: Results-based financing (RBF) significantly increased prenatal care visits, first-trimester care, facility births, and professional delivery assistance, while reducing C-section rates and reducing inequality of opportunity in these maternal health services.
mod_finding: RBF was associated with a reduction in C-section rates by 1.3 percentage points.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 2005/2006, 2010/2011, and 2015 Zimbabwe demographic and health surveys.
